Sureshwar Thakur, J. (Oral)
1.

The notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act of 1894')
became issued on 1.1.2002 (Annexure P-1), which became succeeded by a declaration made on 30.12.2002 under Section 6 of the Act of 1894 (Annexure P-2).
In pursuance thereto, an award was made on 29.12.2004 (Annexure P-7).

2. However, at the outset, initially the raising of the instant writ petition much belatedly therefrom,
inasmuch as in the year 2018, engenders an inference from this Court, that therebys the instant writ petition is ridden with the gross pervasive stains of delay and laches.
Resultantly, the instant writ petition is required to be declared as a completely misconstituted petition.

sentences.text:
Be that as it may, the learned counsel for the petitioners has argued, that in terms of Section 24(2)
of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act of 2013'), the petitioners become entitled to receive a lapsing declaration from this Court vis-a-vis the subject lands.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 1 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:896906-DB 4
. However, the above made argument is not amenable to become accepted by this Court.

The reason for making the above inference becomes stemmed from the factum, that the present petitioners would be entitled to coax this Court to declare the launching of the acquisition proceedings under the Act of 1894, to thus become lapsed, but only when the respondent-State rather had completely failed to, in terms of the verdict rendered by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority versus Manohar Lal and others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129, adduce sufficient/clinching discharging evidence, in respect of the duo parameters, inasmuch as, (i) qua rapat possession being made over the acquired lands, (ii) and, qua the compensation, as became determined by the Collector concerned, becoming deposited for therebys its becoming available for being released to the land losers concerned, besides the said events evidently happening before the coming into force of the Act of 2013.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority versus Manohar Lal and others, reported in (2020) 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. However, a reading of the paragraph 5 of the said reply on affidavit submitted to the instant petition by the respondents concerned, reveals, that prior to coming into force the Act of 20 2013,
not only the rapat possession over the acquired lands became assumed through rapat No. 445 dated 29.12.2004, but also the compensation, as became determined under the impugned award was tendered in quick spontaneity to the rendition of the award thereby making it available for disbursement thereof to the land losers concerned.

Consequently, therebys there is adduction of satisfactory discharging evidence at the instance of the acquiring authority vis-a-vis the duo parameters (supra), as spelt out by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority's case (supra), wherebys the petitioners become disentitled to claim the making of a lapsing declaration in terms of Section 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:896906-DB 24(2) of the Act of 2013.

6. Now insofar as the claim reared in the instant writ petition, that the acquiring authority has discriminated against the present petitioners inasmuch as, theirs declining to exempt or release the subject lands from acquisition, despite the fact, that the acquiring authority had caused releases of the lands covered within the notification (supra), thus to the similarly situated land losers concerned, rather is concerned.
7. However, even the above submission is completely bereft of any vigour.

The reason for forming the above conclusion stems from the fact, that there are clear, and, candid speakings in paragraph 2 of the reply on affidavit, furnished to the instant petition, that the present petitioners had raised objections under Section 5-A of the Act of 1894 before the authority concerned, and, their objections became accepted.
Resultantly, the petitioners' land bearing killa No. 49//4/4(1K-16M) became de-notified from acquisition.

sentences.text: Since the learned counsel for the petitioners does not dispute the fact, that in the said objections the subject lands became omitted to be included.

The sequel of the omission (supra), is that,
therebys since there was waiver and abandonment of the opportunity earlier purveyed to the land losers concerned.

Resultantly, in the face of the above waiver and abandonment of an earlier opportunity, thus by the petitioners or their omission to include the subject lands in the objections filed under Section 5-A of the Act of 1894, concomitantly results in theirs estoppingly acquiescing to the validity of acquisition, as made qua the subject lands.

9. Conspicuously also since it has been stated, in the reply on affidavit, placed on record by the learned State counsel, that the subject 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:896906-DB lands are an integral component of the layout plans, thereby when they are facilitating the relevant public purposes.
Consequently, when public purpose than the ill individualistic interest is rather to be furthered.
Resultantly, this Courts finds no merit in the instant petition, and, is constrained to dismiss it.
10. Accordingly, the instant petition is dismissed.
11. Pending application(s), if any, is/are also disposed of.
